owner_request: Every content project has its own folder in the ChatGPT Library; store all new content, work, reports and artifacts only in the correct project folder.

routing.other_content: Use existing explicit Content/<project-name> folders, not a generalized Checkpoints or Current folder

subfolders.releases: Releases (if needed, never label WIP FINAL)

mandatory_workflow: Resolve exact owner workstream before any Library save or move
Check folder exists, and create it if missing
Save into Content/<owner-project>/<appropriate-subfolder>; never generic root Current/Checkpoints/Final when project owner is known
After each upload/move, read back the actual Library path and stable library_file_id
Preserve original files, stable identities, source fidelity and runtime authorities; never delete duplicates without explicit authorization and exact comparison
Maintain a Git-tracked relocation index for moved historical checkpoint files so old hard-coded library_path breadcrumbs can be reconciled
Do not move mixed/shared A1/A2/B1 audio or coursebook sources out of German-Flashcards-Reference-Library/07_CEFR_COURSEBOOKS; reference source in place
Do not conflate Menschen-A2 (24 lesson project) with Menschen-A2-Verben (independent verb project)
Library move does not confer linguistic PASS, currentness, FINAL, Stage5/6/7 or app import success
If Library upload fails storage limit, disclose and keep an accessible chat artifact if present; do not silently fall back to wrong folder, overwrite, or delete
source_of_truth: GitHub bootstrap/checkpoints determine content authority; Library placement determines personal file organization, not content validation.
